gaps.sentence: Despite ___ three times, he didn't give up.
She avoided ___ about the incident for weeks.
gaps.explanation: 'Avoid' is always followed by the -ing form.

gaps.sentence: We mustn't miss ___ this exhibition — it ends on Sunday.
She was on the verge of ___ up her job to sail around the world.
gaps.explanation: 'On the verge of' ends in a preposition, so the gerund follows.

gaps.sentence: I look forward to ___ your suggestions at the meeting.
It's no use ___ to start the engine — the battery is completely flat.
gaps.explanation: 'It's no use' is followed by a gerund.

gaps.sentence: He spent months ___ the application, only to be rejected in minutes.
gaps.explanation: 'Spend time doing something' takes the gerund.
